summary: Defines the L2VPN Network Model (L2NM), a YANG model for managing the provisioning of Layer 2 VPN services within a network such as a service provider network. It complements the L2VPN Service Model (L2SM) by offering a network-centric view, meant for use by a network controller. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: A customer asks for a private link, and the provider's controller needs a detailed internal plan to build it. This gives a standard form for writing that internal plan.

questions: what is the l2vpn network model
yang model for layer 2 vpn provisioning
subtitle: A YANG model that lets a network controller describe Layer 2 VPN services from the provider's own point of view.

tldr.problem: Customers order Layer 2 VPN services through a customer-facing model (the L2SM), but a service provider's controller needs a network-centric description of the same service in order to configure devices.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9291 defines the L2VPN Network Model (L2NM), a YANG module organized as profiles, services, nodes and network accesses. It also defines a module for Ethernet segments and the first versions of two IANA-maintained modules for BGP Layer 2 encapsulation types and pseudowire types.
tldr.outcome: A service orchestrator can ask a network controller to create, change, delete and retrieve L2VPN services using one standard model, covering VPLS, VPWS and several EVPN flavors.

facts.label: VPN types
facts.value: vpls, vpws, vpws-evpn, pbb-evpn, mpls-evpn, vxlan-evpn

today: RFC 9291 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2022. According to its metadata it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: What the L2VPN Network Model Is
sections.content:
RFC 8466 defines the L2VPN Service Model (L2SM), used between customers and service providers to order Layer 2 VPN services. RFC 9291 complements it with the L2VPN Network Model (L2NM), a network-centric view of the same service that stays inside the provider. It is meant to be used by a network controller to derive the configuration information that is sent to network devices.

The L2NM is scoped for several kinds of Layer 2 VPN: Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS, RFC 4761 and RFC 4762), Virtual Private Wire Service (VPWS), and EVPN flavors including VPWS EVPN (RFC 8214), PBB-EVPN, EVPN over MPLS (RFC 7432) and EVPN over VXLAN. It is designed to be extended to future flavors.

The document also defines a module for managing Ethernet segments and the initial versions of two IANA-maintained modules, iana-bgp-l2-encaps and iana-pseudowire-types. Relying on IANA-maintained modules means new types can be handled without being limited to a fixed set of identities inside the L2NM itself. The models follow the Network Management Datastore Architecture and reuse the common VPN module from RFC 9181.
sections.eli5: The customer fills in a simple order form. The provider needs a much more detailed technical plan. This document is the template for the technical plan.

sections.title: Where the L2NM Fits in the Architecture
sections.content:
The RFC expands the architecture from RFC 8466 by splitting the orchestration box into three parts: Service Orchestration, Network Orchestration and Domain Orchestration. The customer service model (for example l2vpn-svc) sits between the customer and service orchestration. The network model, l2vpn-ntw together with l2vpn-es, sits between service orchestration and network orchestration. Below that are network configuration models and device configuration models, reaching devices through NETCONF or the command-line interface.

A customer does not have to use the L2SM. The RFC lists other ways to request a service that may trigger an L2NM, such as an IP Connectivity Provisioning Profile, an enhanced VPN service or an IETF network slice service. Both models may also be used in the Abstraction and Control of TE Networks (ACTN) framework (RFC 8453), where the L2NM is used between the Multi-Domain Service Coordinator and its children.

The L2NM is not a customer service model and not a device model. How it is used to derive device-specific actions is implementation specific.
sections.eli5: There is a chain of helpers. The first one talks to the customer, the next plans the network, and the last ones set up each machine. The L2NM is the note passed between the first two helpers.

sections.title: Ethernet Segments
sections.content:
The ietf-ethernet-segment module manages Ethernet segments (ES) for EVPN services. An ES is the set of Ethernet links a customer site uses to connect to one or more provider edge routers. Each segment has a unique name, which the L2NM can reference from a VPN network access.

The Ethernet Segment Identifier (ESI) can be configured directly or assigned automatically, with or without a named pool. The supported ESI types are esi-type-0-operator, esi-type-1-lacp, esi-type-2-bridge, esi-type-3-mac, esi-type-4-router-id and esi-type-5-asn. Automatically generated values can be read back.

The module also covers the redundancy mode (Single-Active or All-Active), designated forwarder election settings including whether election is revertive and a wait timer, split-horizon filtering, a PBB backbone source MAC address, and the list of member interfaces.
sections.eli5: An Ethernet segment is the bundle of cables that joins one office to the provider. Giving the bundle a name and a number makes it easy to point at it later.

sections.title: Structure of the L2NM Module
sections.content:
The ietf-l2vpn-ntw module has two main containers. vpn-profiles holds identifiers of provider-defined profiles for external connectivity, encryption, QoS, BFD, forwarding and routing. The exact content of these profiles is local to each provider; the model only carries identifiers so that local policies can be bound.

vpn-services holds one vpn-service per L2VPN, identified by vpn-id, which is meaningful only locally in the network controller. A service has a VPN type (vpls, vpws, vpws-evpn, pbb-evpn, mpls-evpn or vxlan-evpn), a topology (hub-spoke, any-to-any or custom), a signaling type, an underlay transport preference, an optional parent service identifier that links back to the order that triggered it, and administrative and operational status.

Each service contains VPN nodes, which are sets of policies applied on a network node. Each node contains VPN network accesses, the interfaces where customer traffic enters. Unlike the L2SM, the L2NM does not model customer sites, only the provider side of the attachment. A network access carries its connection properties (such as encapsulation, LAG and tag rewrite), service parameters such as MTU, bandwidth, QoS and MAC policies, Ethernet service OAM, and a group and precedence used to mark primary and secondary accesses.
sections.eli5: The plan has levels: the whole service, then each router that takes part, then each plug on the router where a customer connects.

sections.title: Global Parameters Profiles
sections.content:
A global-parameters-profile defines reusable settings for one L2VPN service. Profiles are defined at the service level, activated at the VPN node level, and may then be used at the VPN network access level. Values adjusted at a lower level take precedence over the global ones.

A profile can hold route distinguisher assignment (direct, from a pool, fully automatic, or none), route target import and export rules, the local autonomous system number, the service MTU, whether CE VLAN IDs and class of service are preserved, control-word negotiation, multicast, and MAC policies. The MAC policies include an address limit with an action when it is exceeded, and MAC loop prevention with a window, frequency and retry timer.
sections.eli5: Think of a settings preset you can reuse. A single router or a single plug can still override a preset value for itself.

sections.title: Signaling Options
sections.content:
The signaling-type chosen on the service says how pseudowires or EVPN membership are set up: bgp-signaling (either l2vpn-bgp or evpn-bgp), ldp-signaling or l2tp-signaling. Table 1 in the RFC limits which options fit each VPN type: VPLS and VPWS allow L2TP, LDP or BGP (l2vpn-bgp), while all the EVPN types use evpn-bgp only.

For BGP, a node can enable BGP auto-discovery with a VPN identifier or, for EVPN, an EVPN type and automatic route target derivation. BGP signaling carries items such as the CE range, pseudowire encapsulation type and VPLS edge identifiers, and for EVPN the service interface type and policies for MAC learning, ingress replication, ARP and ND proxying and BUM handling.

LDP and L2TP share common parameters such as an Attachment Group Identifier, a Source Attachment Individual Identifier and a list of peers with Target Attachment Individual Identifiers. With LDP, only Ethernet and Ethernet tagged mode are supported.
sections.eli5: There are different ways for routers to tell each other who is in the private network. The plan has a place to say which way to use and to fill in the details.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are meant to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF, with SSH and TLS as the mandatory-to-implement secure transports, and access can be restricted using the Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM).

Writable nodes are sensitive. The vpn-profiles container can influence routing policies, QoS policies and encryption properties, and is tagged nacm:default-deny-write. For ethernet-segments and vpn-services, an attacker with access could delete a running service, change attributes such as QoS or bandwidth, create a service, add a network access, or redirect traffic to an unauthorized node. The RFC suggests monitoring and tracking configuration changes.

Some readable nodes are also sensitive: customer-name and ip-connection could expose privacy-related information about a customer. The two IANA-maintained modules only define identities and expose no writable or state data.
sections.eli5: The plan controls real customer connections, so only trusted people should be allowed to change it or read the private parts.

sections.title: Examples in the Appendix
sections.content:
Appendix A shows JSON message bodies for six cases: BGP-based VPLS, BGP-based VPWS with LDP signaling, LDP-based VPLS, a VPWS-EVPN service instance, automatic ESI assignment, and VPN network access precedence.

The last example places two network accesses in one VPN node. Both are bound to the same group identifier, and the precedence value marks one as primary and the other as secondary.
sections.eli5: The back of the document has filled-in sample forms so you can see how a real plan looks.
